highlights:
## Haiti will return to the World Cup after more than half a century with a generation dreaming of shocking the football world.
[...]
Haiti will arrive at the 2026 FIFA World Cup as one of the tournament’s most emotional and surprising stories. After decades away from football’s biggest stage, Les Grenadiers will finally return to compete among the world’s best national teams.
[...]
With an athletic, fast, and increasingly experienced generation playing in international leagues, Haiti will try to prove it can be much more than just a participant and potentially become one of the tournament’s surprise teams.
[...]
Haiti qualified for the 2026 FIFA World Cup after finishing second in Concacaf Qualifying Group C.
[...]
The Caribbean side collected nine points thanks to three victories and one defeat, finishing ahead of Saint Lucia, Aruba, and Barbados to secure its return to the World Cup.
[...]
to write a new historic chapter for Haitian football.
[...]
Sébastien Migné will lead Haiti at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The French coach has extensive experience working with African and Caribbean national teams, building organized and competitive squads.
[...]
Under his leadership, Haiti developed into a far more defensively solid and confident national team capable of competing against stronger international opponents.
[...]
Wilson Isidor will arrive at the 2026 World Cup as one of Haiti’s main attacking threats and one of the most promising players of this Caribbean generation.
[...]
The Sunderland center forward stands out because of his pace, physical strength, and ability to attack spaces behind opposing defenses. His constant movement and aggressiveness inside the box also make him a key piece of Les Grenadiers’ attack.
[...]
Haiti will need the best version of Isidor to compete against more experienced World Cup nations.

- Weakness: limited collective experience at the highest level
- Playing style: quick transitions, aggressive pressing, and direct attacks

results.title: Haiti World Cup 2026: Les Grenadiers Squad, Migné & Group C Guide | Fanorate
highlights:
captain Johny Placide
[...]
Haiti are the great romance of the 2026 World Cup. “Les Grenadiers” return to the global stage for only the second time in their history, and the first since their debut at West Germany 1974 — a 52-year wait. For a nation that has endured profound hardship, qualification is a moment of immense national pride, celebrated across Haiti and throughout its large diaspora communities in North America and Europe.
[...]
Haiti sealed qualification by topping their final qualifying group, clinching the berth with a decisive win over Nicaragua on the final matchday — played in Curaçao because of instability at home. The squad is a celebration of the Haitian diaspora: nearly every player developed overseas, with only a single home-based player (midfielder Woodensky Pierre of Violette AC) in the group. At its heart is 38-year-old captain and goalkeeper Johny Placide, finally reaching a World Cup after nearly every recent cycle. It is a story of perseverance on a national and personal scale.
[...]
Realistically, Haiti are the outsiders of Group C, sharing it with five-time champions Brazil and 2022 semi-finalists Morocco. Simply being there is already historic.
[...]
The genuine targets are competitive, respectable performances, a first-ever World Cup point or goal in the modern era, and using the expanded 48-team format to chase a famous result. Anything beyond the group stage would be one of the tournament’s all-time fairytales.
[...]
on this stage
[...]
Expect Haiti to set up pragmatically: a compact, disciplined defensive block designed to frustrate superior opponents, with quick, direct counter-attacks aimed at their physical strikers (Pierrot, Nazon). Migné’s side will likely prioritise organisation, low-block resilience and set-piece threat, looking to turn moments of individual quality and transition speed into rare but dangerous chances.
[...]
- One of the great feel-good stories of the entire tournament.
- A genuine underdog you can’t help but root for against the giants.
- Passionate, colourful support from Haiti’s diaspora in host cities.
- The chance to witness history — Haiti’s first World Cup goal or point in the modern era.
- Compelling personal journeys, from Placide’s patience to Pierrot’s rise.
[...]
Group-stage exit — but a goal on the World Cup stage and a nation united in pride.
[...]
Haiti are likely to finish bottom of Group C against this calibre of opposition. But in an expanded, unpredictable format, a hard-fought draw or a shock result is not impossible. Realistic success looks like a competitive showing, a goal on the World Cup stage and a nation united in pride — regardless of the points.
